title: Analysis of De Novo Synthesized Proteins
author: Anne Zemella
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqnxmvfn

steps.title: Collect translation and microsomal fractions
steps.instruction: After the translation reaction, collect two 3 µL aliquots of the translation mixture, centrifuge the remaining mixture at 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 15 min, collect two 3 µL aliquots of the supernatant, resuspend the microsomal fraction in an equal volume of PBS (matching the translation‑mix volume), and collect two 3 µL aliquots of the microsomal fraction.

steps.title: Precipitate proteins with TCA
steps.instruction: To each 3 µL aliquot add 3 mL trichloroacetic acid (TCA), incubate in a water bath at 80 °C for 15 min, then store the tubes on ice for 30 min or overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Vacuum‑filter and wash precipitates
steps.instruction: Apply each TCA‑treated mixture to a vacuum filtration system to retain radio‑labeled protein and remove non‑incorporated ^14C‑leucine; wash each filter twice with TCA followed by two washes with acetone, and dry the filters under the hood.

steps.title: Scintillation counting of protein filters
steps.instruction: Transfer each dried filter into a scintillation vial, overlay with 3 mL scintillation cocktail, incubate with gentle shaking for 1 h, then count radioactivity in a scintillation counter.

steps.title: Select aliquot for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Take either a 5 µL aliquot of fluorescently labeled protein (Bodipy‑TMR‑Lysine) or a 10 µL aliquot of site‑specifically labeled protein (non‑canonical amino acid) from each prepared sample.

steps.title: Dry protein pellets
steps.instruction: Dry the collected pellets for 1 h at 45 °C in a thermomixer set to 1 000 rpm.

steps.title: Resuspend and load SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Resuspend each dried pellet in 20 µL SDS‑PAGE sample buffer, load onto a pre‑cast 10 % SDS‑PAGE gel together with a fluorescently labeled protein ladder, and run the gel under standard conditions.

steps.title: Fluorescence imaging of gel
steps.instruction: Transfer the completed gel to a fluorescence imaging system; detect Bodipy‑TMR‑lysine bands with a 532 nm laser and 580 nm emission filter, and detect Sulfo‑Cy5 bands with excitation at 633 nm and emission at 670 nm.

steps.title: Dry gel and phosphor‑screen exposure
steps.instruction: Dry the gel for 1 h at 70 °C using a unigel dryer, then expose the dried gel on a phosphor screen for at least 3 days before reading out with a multi‑mode imager.

steps.title: Prepare samples for confocal microscopy
steps.instruction: Mix 5 µL fluorescently labeled protein from the microsomal fraction with 20 µL PBS, add the mixture to a μ‑Ibidi slide, and fix the slide.

steps.title: Set microscope optics and settings
steps.instruction: Use a plan‑apochromat objective (60× or 100×); microsomal structures are 1–10 µm in diameter. Adjust the beam path for the dye (e.g., Cy5 excited at 633 nm, emission collected >670 nm; FITC preset). Then adjust laser intensity, gain, focus, and pinhole according to the sample.

steps.title: Acetone precipitation before imaging
steps.instruction: To each 5 µL or 10 µL aliquot add 45 µL water and 150 µL cold acetone, incubate on ice for 15 min, keep samples protected from light, centrifuge at 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 min, and discard the supernatant.
